bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to the authority of Congress and the States to regulate contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections and to enact public financing systems for political campaigns.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The amendment would reshape campaign finance law, directly affecting lobbying firms and attorneys who advise on election spending and compliance.
Advocacy organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new regulatory authority over their fundraising and expenditures.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit them to create public financing systems for campaigns and to treat corporations differently from individual people, including by prohibiting corporations from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-82.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill creates new procedural pathways and limits defenses in civil litigation, expanding the scope and duration of claims that law firms may pursue or defend.
Museums and cultural institutions that hold or exhibit artwork are directly affected by expanded liability and procedural rules for restitution claims.
Banks and auction houses that handle art transactions or hold art as collateral face potential claims if works in their possession are subject to restitution.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and other property taken during Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945. It makes it easier to sue foreign governments and defendants located anywhere in the United States, and it blocks certain legal defenses that courts have used to dismiss these claims, such as arguments that too much time has passed. The changes apply to cases already filed as well as future ones.

plain.whoItTouches: People who have been the victim of a crime.

bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-12.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on social media platforms and user-generated content websites.
New criminal prohibitions and mandatory restitution provisions would generate litigation and enforcement work related to intimate image publication.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. Social media platforms and similar websites would be required to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a complaint from the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Holocaust Education and Antisemitism Lessons Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 470.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill directs a study of curriculum requirements and instructional materials used in public schools, directly affecting education publishers and curriculum developers who produce Holocaust education materials.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to conduct a study and report to Congress on how Holocaust education is taught in public elementary and secondary schools across the country. The study would examine whether states and local school districts require Holocaust education, what standards and curriculum requirements exist, and what instructional materials are being used. The bill does not itself mandate Holocaust education or change school curricula; it only requires the museum to gather and report information on current practices.

districtAwards.description: FY26 ANNUAL SUSTAINMENT CONTRACT - UCA AWARD

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (CT DEEP). THE RECIPIENT WILL IMPLEMENT GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTION PROGRAMS, POLICIES, PROJECTS, AND MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN A PRIORITY CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (PCAP) DEVELOPED UNDER A CLIMATE POLLUTION REDUCTION GRANTS (CPRG) PLANNING GRANT. ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED THROUGH THIS GRANT WILL BENEFIT ALL RESIDENTS OF AND VISITORS TO CONNECTICUT, MAINE, MASSACHUSETTS, NEW HAMPSHIRE AND RHODE ISLAND THROUGH FOUR MAIN OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENTATION OF AMBITIOUS MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SIGNIFICANT CUMULATIVE GHG REDUCTIONS BY 2030 AND BEYOND; PURSUIT OF MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SUBSTANTIAL COMMUNITY BENEFITS, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; COMPLEMENTING OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO MAXIMIZE THESE GHG REDUCTIONS AND COMMUNITY BENEFITS; AND, PURSUIT OF INNOVATIVE POLICIES AND PROGRAMS THAT ARE REPLICABLE AND CAN BE 'SCALED UP' ACROSS MULTIPLE JURISDICTIONS. ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE VARIOUS INITIATIVES INTENDED TO RAPIDLY ACCELERATE ADOPTION OF COLD-CLIMATE AIR-SOURCE HEAT PUMPS (ASHPS), HEAT PUMP WATER HEATERS (HPWHS), AND GROUND SOURCE HEAT PUMPS (GSHPS) IN SINGLE-FAMILY AND MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS IN CONNECTICUT, MAINE, MASSACHUSETTS, NEW HAMPSHIRE, AND RHODE ISLAND. THESE INITIATIVES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH THREE PROGRAM PILLARS OR 'HUBS': THE MARKET HUB, INNOVATION HUB, AND RESOURCE HUB.  

THROUGH THE MARKET HUB, THE RECIPIENT WILL WORK WITH CONTRACTORS AND PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS TO PROVIDE PER-UNIT MIDSTREAM INCENTIVES FOR QUALIFYING ASHPS, HPWHS, AND GSHPS VIA DISTRIBUTORS. THE RECIPIENT WILL ALSO CONDUCT CONTRACTOR TRAINING ON REGIONALLY RELEVANT TOPICS, SUCH AS COLD-CLIMATE HEAT PUMPS AND WHOLE-HOME INSTALLATIONS, TO DRIVE CONSISTENT INSTALLATION PRACTICES. WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS TO GROW THE CONTRACTOR BASE, WITH A FOCUS ON PROMOTING JOB CREATION AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES (LIDACS), WILL BE DEVELOPED AS WELL.  

ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED THROUGH THE INNOVATION HUB INCLUDE 1 OR 2 LARGE-SCALE, MULTIYEAR STATE INITIATIVES TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC STATE PRIORITIES AND DEVELOP SCALABLE SOLUTIONS TO OVERCOME BARRIERS FOR LIDACS; ANNUAL 'QUICK START GRANTS' FOR COMMUNITY-BASED PILOT PROJECTS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO HEAT PUMPS FOR LIDACS; AND STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT TO ENSURE COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT IN THE DESIGN OF THESE PROGRAMS. 

THROUGH THE RESOURCE HUB, THE RECIPIENT AND ITS PARTNERS WILL COLLECT AND SHARE AGGREGATE OR ANONYMIZED DATA ON HEAT PUMP MARKETS AND PROGRAM PARTICIPATION; SHARE RESOURCES FOR CONSUMER AND CONTRACTOR EDUCATION; AND OFFER ADDITIONAL LIDAC-SPECIFIC OUTREACH AND RESOURCES. STIPENDS WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO GROUPS REPRESENTING LIDACS TO ENCOURAGE COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:KEY DELIVERABLES INCLUDE SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND A DETAILED FINAL REPORT TO EPA; A QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRESS PLAN (QAPP), IF DEEMED NECESSARY BY EPA; ANNUAL PROGRAM EVALUATIONS BY A THIRD-PARTY PROGRAM EVALUATOR (BEGINNING IN MONTH 23 OF THE PROJECT); AND ANNUAL REPORTS TO STAKEHOLDERS DESCRIBING RESULTS FOR THE MARKET HUB AND INNOVATION HUB (ALSO BEGINNING IN MONTH 23). REPORTS FOR THE INNOVATION HUB WILL INCLUDE INFORMATION ON HEAT PUMPS INSTALLED (INCLUDING DATA ON INSTALLATIONS IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES), BARRIERS OVERCOME, INCUMBENT SYSTEMS REPLACED, AND SCALABLE SOLUTIONS IDENTIFIED. REPORTS TO EPA WILL DESCRIBE ACTUAL GHG EMISSIONS REDUCED AND REPORT ON THE RECIPIENT'S PROGRESS TOWARD ACHIEVING OTHER OUTPUTS AND OUTCOMES DESCRIBED IN THE WORKPLAN.
